Extract a centroid total-ion or selected-ion trace

Source: R/acquisition-extract.R
measure_ms_trace.Rd

Extract one explicit polarity and MS level from one declared MS stream. Centroid intensities are summed in their original point order. A closed mz_range selects an inclusive extracted-ion window in the stream's declared m/z unit; NULL extracts a total-ion trace.

Usage

measure_ms_trace(x, stream_id, polarity, ms_level, mz_range = NULL)

Arguments

x

A validated measure_acquisition.

stream_id

One exact MS stream identifier.

polarity

One of "positive" or "negative".

ms_level

One positive MS level.

mz_range

NULL for a total-ion trace, or a two-value closed m/z interval in the stream's declared unit.

Value

An ordinary tibble with one row per selected scan. The columns are scan_id, scan_index, source_scan_id, retention_time, value, status, selected_points, saturation_unknown, and .point_indices. The processing attribute records the declared extraction parameters. The returned table does not require a monotonic time axis; converting it to a scalar record requires that record's checks.

Details

One stream, polarity, and MS level must be selected explicitly. A scan whose unknown settings could match the requested combination is ambiguous and causes an error. Unknown settings on scans excluded by another known selector do not block the calculation. An empty selection is an error.

Selected rows follow their declared scan_index, retaining repeated or nonmonotonic retention times. Times must be known and finite and the stream must declare a time unit. XIC bounds require a known declared m/z unit. No units are converted and no samples, polarities or MS levels are pooled.

Acquired selected scans must declare centroid representation. Every m/z in those scans must be finite and positive, including points outside an XIC window. Selected intensities must be finite and nonnegative or ordinary NA; NaN, infinities, negative values and unrepresentable sums cause errors. Unselected intensities do not contribute to an XIC. Duplicate m/z points contribute separately, in their original order.

Missingness and saturation

The following statuses describe the declared centroid calculation:

  • missing_scan: an explicitly missing scan yields NA, with no points.

  • empty_scan: an acquired-empty centroid spectrum yields zero.

  • empty_window: a nonempty spectrum with no XIC matches yields zero.

  • saturated: any selected point declared saturated yields NA.

  • missing_intensity: any selected ordinary NA yields NA.

  • calculated: the selected finite intensities were summed.

Saturation takes precedence over ordinary missing intensity. Invalid selected numerical states still cause errors before either policy is applied. saturation_unknown independently records whether any selected mask entry is unknown; it is not silently treated as FALSE. A calculated value does not certify an instrument, method, absence of saturation, or analyte identity.

Contributor links and processing

.point_indices retains every selected original point position, including those responsible for an NA result. Together with scan_id, these indices link each output row to its retained acquisition input. They are not source file line numbers. Source record ordinals remain in the raw scan's .source_rows and original source scan identifiers remain opaque text.

The processing attribute is a named list recording version 1, the operation, package version, explicit stream/injection/channel/source IDs and available source digest, selectors, bounds, units, centroid sum, propagation policies and absence of synchronization. Unknown source evidence remains unknown. Keep this metadata and contributor links with the raw acquisition. A scalar record export alone does not preserve many-to-one extraction ancestry.

Profile spectra may be stored but are not calculated here: an unweighted profile-point sum depends on sampling density and is not physical integration. This function performs no centroiding, interpolation, binning or annotation.

See also

measure_acquisition()
